Subject: Nimbus observability onboarding: signal census & runbook kickoff

Hi Laura / team —

Thanks for taking this forward. We're excited to start the observability onboarding with Redwood. Attached is a first-pass telemetry spec (NIM-telemetry-spec.xlsx) that our infra team exported from our staging environment. High level asks:

- Confirm which dashboards we should prioritize for go-live (latency, error-rate, request-paths).
- Map tracing hooks we need instrumented for cross-service traces of the inference path (gateway -> routing -> model pool).
- Agree an error taxonomy so alerts are actionable (user-impacting, backlog-bumping, infra).
- Draft a runbook template we can own in Nimbus that codifies escalation paths and triage steps.

Can Redwood share a recommended signal census template and a runbook template we can use to align teams? We're targeting a staging cutover the week of Feb 15.

Attachments: NIM-telemetry-spec.xlsx

Thanks —
Sophie Grant
VP, Platform Engineering
Nimbus Health Systems

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>

Cc: ben_carter, marissa_cole, jonas_weber
Date: Tue, 26 Jan 2027 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Nimbus observability onboarding: signal census & runbook kickoff

Hi Sophie —

Great to meet you (virtually). Thanks for sending the telemetry dump. We've reviewed the sheet and sketched a proposed prioritization for the staging cutover. I'm attaching a small runbook template we use for onboarding customers (runbook-template.md). I'll summarize our first-pass recommendations below and suggest a short working session to lock the mutual action plan.

Priority dashboards (start):
- Inference latency breakdown: p50/p95/p99 by model variant and request path
- Errors by downstream: model OOM, tokenization failures, routing misroutes
- Request rate + cold-starts (by pool)

Tracing hooks to add (minimal initially):
- Gateway request id propagation header (x-nimbus-req-id)
- Start/stop for routing decision (route->pool selection)
- Model invocation start/finish with model_version and quantization flags

Proposed error taxonomy (3 tiers):
1) Critical: user-facing generation failures (500s / blank responses) — paging to oncall
2) Degraded: elevated latency or increased p99 latency — slack alert to SRE + CS
3) Informational: model quality regressions / prompt errors — batched notifications and tracking in ticket queue

Action items (LAURA / REDWOOD):
- We will populate the signal census template and share a prefilled version by Fri, Jan 29 (laura).
- Ben will draft alert thresholds based on staging baseline (ben).
- Marissa will coordinate the runbook ownership with your CS lead (marissa).

Proposed meeting: Thu, Jan 28 10:00am PT — 30 minutes to run through the MAP and owners. Can you confirm?

Attachments: runbook-template.md

Best,
Laura Bennett
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett, marissa_cole, Sophie Grant <sophie@nimbushs.com>, NimBus Implementation <impl-team@nimbushs.com>
Date: Thu, 28 Jan 2027 08:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Nimbus observability onboarding: signal census & runbook kickoff

+1 on the meeting — confirmed for Thu 10am PT. Quick operational note from my side:

- For alert routing, we should map alerts to service owners by Kubernetes namespace + model-pool tag. If Nimbus can add a model_pool label to the metrics and traces payload, we can attach routing rules automatically in Redwood Console.
- For the staging baseline I'll need 48 hours of traffic profiles (your NIM dump had a 6 hour slice). Can the impl-team push a 48h csv or grant read access to the bucket?

Example thresholds I'm going to propose (draft):
- p99 latency > 2.5x baseline for 5m => degraded (Slack to SRE)
- error rate > 0.5% over 10m => critical (pager) if it correlates with 5xx from model pool

Marissa — can you pick the initial runbook owner on the Nimbus side? We should avoid ambiguous ownership for paging.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
